claims.claim: Wolfe argues a long work must show its characters earning their living or it acquires a creeping sense of unreality.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, 'Nor the Summers as Golden' (2007), Gwern.net

claims.claim: Wolfe claims almost everyone is interesting while at work, even when the work itself is not.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, 'Nor the Summers as Golden' (2007), Gwern.net
claims.quote: virtually everyone is interesting at work

claims.claim: Wolfe gives half a million words as the working size of the multivolume work he describes.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, 'Nor the Summers as Golden' (2007), Gwern.net

claims.claim: Wolfe reports telling a beginner to post a sign reading I AM GOING TO TELL YOU SOMETHING COOL facing the desk.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, 'Nor the Summers as Golden' (2007), Gwern.net
claims.quote: I AM GOING TO TELL YOU SOMETHING COOL

claims.claim: Wolfe's closing advice separates manner, to be learned from the masters, from matter, which must be the writer's own.
claims.quote: For the manner, study the masters; for the matter

claims.claim: Wolfe closes the piece with a figure making ink out of smoke-blackened blood that must be the writer's own.
claims.quote: Blood blacked with smoke's a good ink

claims.claim: Wolfe tells the aspiring fantasist he will be measured against Homer.
claims.quote: Work hard, and recollect you'll be measured against Homer

claims.claim: Wolfe said he writes sequentially and then rewrites repeatedly rather than composing out of order.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, live chat-channel Q&A transcript (1996)
claims.quote: I write sequentially, and then go back and rewrite

claims.claim: Wolfe confirmed Nabokov was somewhat an influence, adding that he came to him late.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, live chat-channel Q&A transcript (1996)
claims.quote: I came to Nabokov somewhat late

claims.claim: Asked what is lost when people take all their stories from television, Wolfe answered that the personal connection with story and myth is lost.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, live chat-channel Q&A transcript (1996)
claims.quote: Any personal connection with story, with myth, is lost

claims.claim: Wolfe called Neil Gaiman the great guru of dialogue.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by David Wilbanks for Hellnotes (2005)

claims.claim: Wolfe classified his own Latro (Soldier) books as historical fantasy.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by David Wilbanks for Hellnotes (2005)
claims.quote: I think I'd call the Soldier

claims.claim: Offering further titles, Wolfe named The Elements of Style alongside an atlas.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by David Wilbanks for Hellnotes (2005)

claims.claim: Wolfe described eight thirty to eleven as his typical daily writing stretch in 2005.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by David Wilbanks for Hellnotes (2005)
claims.quote: Eight thirty to eleven is pretty typical
claims.page: answer on an average work day

claims.claim: Aramini says Wolfe's planted clues rest on objective external fact rather than on subjective information.
claims.quote: not subjective information but objective fact
claims.page: answer on surprises in his research
